decoration_note: Woodcuts painted over in gold and colours. On a1r, f2r, h3r, l7r, and m2r full borders are supplied in gold and colours, by a close follower of Matteo Felice (fl. 1467-1493), perhaps a member of his workshop. On a1r and f2r the border contains putti, a peacock, a hare, foliate decoration in blue, purple, and green, filigree and gold bezants, all enclosed within a frame of gold and another of blue. On h3r and l7r the border contains also a bird; on m2r there is a stag and one putto wears a breastplate.  Main initials contain the following miniatures: on e7v Virgin and child, on f2r David praying, on h3r a coffin covered by a drape, behind stand a priest and fours monks praying, with a tall pole with cross on top, on l7r Christ on the cross, surrounded by the instruments of the Passion, on m2r Descent of the Holy Spirit. The initials on e7v, f2r, h3r, l7r, m2r, are supplied in purple with green foliate edges and blue inside the letter, all with white penwork, within a gold ground, and with floral extension from the letter into the margin in blue, purple, green, and gold bezants. Other main initials are supplied in gold on a shaped blue ground with white penwork, the area enclosed by the letter is purple with white penwork, or the reverse; sometimes it can also consist of a chequered ground red and blue; occasionally a pen extension from the letter forms foliate decoration and gold bezants. In the calendar the letters «KL» are supplied in gold with violet penwork. On a1r coat of arms in the lower panel of the border; azure, a cock proper crested and jellopped, on a chief argent two flowers(?) gules.

manuscript_note: Additions to the calendar in a sixteenth-century hand: 17 Sept. «Stigmata sancti Francisci»; in the upper margin of [A9r] «Sancti Caroli Cardinalis Borromei Archiep Mediolan. »; next to s Prosdocimi (7 Nov.) added «Patavini», all in the same hand. Bound at the end are nine parchment leaves of manuscript prayers and suffrages, with painted miniatures of St George killing the dragon; St Jacobus ap; St Augustine; St Sebastianus; Leonardus cf; Cristophoro; Antonio cf; the crucifixion, behind, a landscape, next, the prayer: «Domine deus meus si feci uel commisi... ». These additions begin with capitals in blue with red penwork decoration. -- More prayers in a later hand, in Latin and in Italian, washed. -- Arabic numerals were added to calendar in an early hand. In the litanies, «Nicolae de Tollentino» was added in the margin between Innocentes and Stephane; «sce Anelle» was added after Ianuari, «sce Iuliane» before Nicolae; a name now erased before Bernarde; «Sancta Anna» before M. Magdalena; «Sta Martha» between Agatha and Clara; all in a contemporary hand, brown ink.

binding_note:
Sixteenth-century parchment; rebacked probably in the eighteenth/nineteenth century with whiter parchment; manuscript title in black ink along the spine, from the tail up: «LIBER PRAECUM AD B. MARIAM VIRG.». The book was restored in the twentieth century; probably at that stage thirteenth-century manuscript parchment bifolia were detached from the inside of the binding and bound as endleaves. Now pastedowns and three further leaves of paper have been inserted at the front and at the end. The original manuscript rear pastedown, to which ξ8 is glued, is now bound at the front. Therefore the original pastedowns have been preserved by the restaurer but have been inverted. The former owners' inscriptions on α1 of the Brevissima introductio, however, suggest that that gathering must have been bound at the front of the Horae since the sixteenth century.    
Two Italian paper labels are found on the front cover: in the lower part of the board, part of a rectangular label with printed numbering: «[missing] | [part of a Roman numeral] | 27» where the printed 7 is corrected to 8 in pen; the second label, in the upper part of the board, is octagonal, edged in a light blue frame «D | V | 15»; both belong to the same collection, probably a local aristocratic family, though we should exclude the possibility that they belong to the library of the seminary itself, in consideration of the same typology (Capital letter | Roman numeral | Arabic numeral); several other sixteenth-century books present the rectangular one, as kindly observed by the Librarian of the Seminary, Dr. Elena Gurrieri.

note: inscription in brown ink in the upper margin of α2r of the Brevissima introductio «Bibliothece Florentine Domus Probationis [...] [...]».

The library of the seminary was created in 1783 with the donation by the Grand Duke of Tuscany Peter Leopold (Vienna 1747-1792) of the book holdings of the suppressed convent of the Cistercians 'del Cestello', rich in fifteenth (74 incunables are now in the library) to seventeenth editions. This book does not present the traditional ownership note «Bibliothecae Cistelli», however the rebinding operation may be responsible for the lack of evidence. Another part of the collection comes from Abbot Ferdinando Ughelli (1594-1670), the famous author of Italia Sacra; therefore this other provenance should not be excluded.

note: Inc.5.E.2.2[2815]: Provenance: Bought from Thomas Toon in July 1888 for £8-0-0, using money from the Rustat Fund (note on front free end paper). First page inscribed 'P: Aerlebout Petrus Aerlebout Pastor in Driel 1682'. A similar inscription on y6r is dated '11 Junij 1682'. At the end of the volume is the inscription 'dit booc hoirt den besloten Conuenten der susteren van Sinte vrselen binnen Cschyedam Hyllegont symon Ians dochter'. Decoration: Principal initials illuminated with pink, blue and green colouring and red pen-flourishes in post-Renaissance style; nineteenth-century? Other initials supplied in alternating blue and red; capital strokes supplied and headings underlined in red. Device hand coloured. UkCU,SSS.19.16: Provenance: Bookplates of Francis Freeling and Samuel Sandars; printed label (1896) of Sandars bequest. In the possession of 'a gentleman at Harlem' in 1756 when it was examined on behalf of Jacob Bryant. No. 1171 in Freeling's sale catalogue (1836). Subsequently lot 202 in the sale of W. Jones Thomas (1891); bought from Ridler by Sandars in December of that year for £7.10s. See The Library, 5th series, II, p. 194-195 and III, p. 65-66. Annotations: Notes on front free end papers in the hands of Freeling and Sandars. On second front fly leaf verso a forged provenance inscription in an eighteenth-century hand: 'Ex Liber [sic] Monasterii Harlamei'. On d6r a further forged inscription in Dutch signed 'Gherard tomasz pieters zoe[n]' purporting to record the purchase of this volume from his cousin 'coster ian zoe[n]'.  MS text in Dutch, probably genuine, on k4v. At the end is a forged colophon, apparently stamped from a block: '[G]epre[n]t toe harlem bi mi laur[en]z ia[n]zon coster. m.cccc.l.' Decoration: Principal initials supplied in blue with flourishes in red and green. Other initials supplied in alternating red and blue. The forged colophon is decorated in a similar style.

note:
on the first verso endleaf his bibliographical note: «4326 Marii Philelphi officiu(m) marie virginis et crucis et sp(irit)us sancti cum septe(m) psalmis et passione in versu thoscano»; on 103v: «Este libro assí enquadernado costo en Venecia 10 beços a dos de hebrero de 1530 y el ducado español vale 280 beços. Esta registrado 4326». In Segura Morera et al.’s catalogue the date given, 1520 instead of 1530, appears to be a typo, as a number of other manuscripts were bought in Venice and the Veneto in 1530 by Colón. 
The first substantial purchases of Colón in Venice occurred in 1521; he had instructed the Genoese merchant and banker Ottaviano Grimaldi (†1576) to ship the books to Seville via Cadiz. Unfortunately they were lost at sea; fortunately, however, they had already been registered and are listed in Hernando Colón, Memorial de los libros naufragados o Registro antiguo o Registrum A (1521, Feb-Nov.), Seville, Bibl. Colombina, MS 10-1-3; JOSÉ FRANCISCO SÁEZ GUILLÉN, Catálogo de manuscritos de la Biblioteca Colombina de Sevilla, Seville, Cabildo de la S.M. Y P.I. Catedral de Sevilla Institución Colombina, 2002, no. 620; KLAUS WAGNER, El itinerario de Hernando Colón segund sus anotaciones. Datos para la biografia del bibliofilo sevillano, «Archivo Hispalense», LXVI, no. 203, 1984 for 1983, pp. 81-99; ID., Hernando Colón: semblanza de un bibliófilo y de su biblioteca en el quinientos aniversario de su nacimiento, in El libro antiguo español. Actas del segundo Coloquio Internacional (Madrid), ed. María Luisa López-Vidriero and Pedro M. Cátedra, Salamanca, Ediciones de la Universidad de Salamanca, Biblioteca nacional de Madrid, Sociedad española de historia del libro, 1992, II, pp. 475-492.
A second trip to Venice took place in 1530, when he bought part of the collection of Marin Sanudo.
price_note: Purchased in Venice in 1530

note:
Colón's library was deposited in 1544 at the Dominican convent of San Pablo, then passed to the Chapter of Seville in 1552. Colón had 15,000 books by the end of his life, with a special interest in vernacular languages, popular literature and cheap printing; JUAN GUILLÉN, Hernando Colón: humanismo y bibliofilia, Sevilla, Fundación José Manuel Lara, 2004, pp. 249-267.
